findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is missing or unmatched
findings.body: The migration unconditionally does execute(...embed_category...)[0]['id'] before copying any hosts. On a default install there is no site_settings row named embed_category (the YAML default is an empty string and is not persisted), so the SELECT returns zero rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises NoMethodError. The same crash happens if the stored value is a slug, an id, a different case, or a deleted category name, because the join is an exact match on categories.name. The uncategorized_category_id fallback on line 15 never runs in that case, and it has the same unchecked [0] access if that row is absent. Every upgrade that hits this aborts the migration and blocks deploy, including sites that never used embedding.

findings.title: Host backfill interpolates SQL and skips normalization
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)", bypassing EmbeddableHost callbacks and quote escaping. The old allow check treated http://eviltrout.com and https://example.com/1234 as the hostname only (URI#host / scheme strip). Those strings are stored verbatim, while EmbeddableHost.record_for_host looks up uri.host (eviltrout.com), so previously working allowlist entries stop matching and embeds start failing with invalid referer after a migration that otherwise succeeds. A value containing a single quote breaks the statement and aborts the migration; because this runs as the migration DB role, a crafted setting can also inject SQL. Blank lines and trailing CR from split("\n") are inserted as-is and will not match either. Use a bound, normalized insert (strip scheme, path, whitespace, downcase) instead of raw interpolation.

findings.title: Imports lose embed_category unless the URL host matches
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import used to pass SiteSetting.embed_category into PostCreator for every imported topic. It now passes only EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url).try(:category_id). When that lookup returns nil or false, category is nil and the new topic is filed in uncategorized. The migration deletes the embed_category site setting and only copies it onto embeddable_hosts rows, so there is no remaining default. Feed polling (Jobs::PollFeed, triggered from TopicRetriever when feed_polling_enabled) imports article URLs that were never required to be iframe allowlist hosts. Sites that set embed_category for RSS/Atom embedding but had a blank embeddable_hosts list lose the category entirely, and any feed item whose host does not exactly match an EmbeddableHost row is created uncategorized. Existing topics are not moved; all future imports are.

findings.title: Allow check does not match hosts the model accepts
findings.body: record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host without downcasing the bind parameter, and before_validation does not downcase the saved host. The format validator is case-insensitive, so Example.com is valid and stored as-is, but a referer or embed URL whose host is example.com fails the query and host_allowed? returns false. The same method ignores the port, while the validator allows example.com:8080 and the callback only strips a scheme and a path, so a saved ported host never equals uri.host. Consequence: legitimate embeds and TopicRetriever fetches are rejected, and TopicEmbed.import assigns no category, for values the admin UI just accepted. Downcase on write and in the query, and decide explicitly whether port is part of the key.

findings.title: Host regex rejects real hostnames the old setting allowed
findings.body: validates_format_of requires a dotted hostname whose final label is [a-z]{2,5} and whose labels are separated by a single hyphen or dot. That rejects localhost, IP addresses, and any TLD longer than five characters (.museum, .photography, .international, and other gTLDs already in use), plus punycode labels that contain '--' (xn--…). The previous embeddable_hosts site setting was a free-form list and allowed those hosts. Admins cannot save them now, so embedding cannot be enabled for those origins. The optional path group in the regex is also unreachable because before_validation strips the path first.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! twice with no presence check. EmbeddableHost.new.valid? or save with a missing host (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host], which can be nil) raises NoMethodError instead of failing validation and returning 422 via render_json_error. There is also no validates_presence_of :host or :category_id, so a record can be valid? with category_id nil even though the column is null: false, and save then raises StatementInvalid rather than a validation error.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
findings.body: update and destroy load the row with where(id: params[:id]).first and immediately use it (save_host sets host.host, destroy calls host.destroy) with no nil check or 404. An unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500. save_host also assumes params[:embeddable_host] is present, so a request without that key 500s the same way. On update, a missing or blank category_id is silently replaced with uncategorized_category_id, so a partial update wipes the category relationship.

findings.title: category_id is not checked and has no foreign key
findings.body: save_host writes whatever category_id is posted, and the migration declares category_id integer null: false with no foreign key or index. A deleted, unknown, or non-numeric id is stored. Category#destroy is not wired to embeddable_hosts, so deleting a category leaves dangling ids. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id to PostCreator, which cannot find the category, and new embedded topics land in uncategorized while the admin UI still shows the host as assigned. belongs_to :category does not validate existence.

findings.title: Hosts are not unique, so category lookup is arbitrary
findings.body: embeddable_hosts.host has no unique index, and EmbeddableHost has no uniqueness validation (case-insensitive or otherwise). After normalization, http://example.com and example.com become the same string and both can be saved, with different category_ids. record_for_host uses where(...).first with no ORDER BY, so topic import and the allow check pick an arbitrary row. Two admins, a retried migration (the INSERT is not idempotent), or duplicate lines in the old setting produce conflicting category assignments for one origin.

findings.title: Plural id hydration throws and drops unresolved ids
findings.body: The new _ids branch in _hydrateEmbedded calls obj[k].map with no check that the value is an array, then always deletes the original key and assigns pluralize(subType), even when _lookupSubType returns undefined. This runs for every payload with __rest_serializer == "1", not only embedding. A null or non-array *_ids attribute throws during store.find/findAll and fails the load. Id lists that are not sideloaded under the naive plural (thing + "s") are replaced with an array of undefined entries and the original ids are discarded. The previous code only rewrote singular _id keys, and only when a match was found.

findings.title: Category and embeddable-host fabricators are swapped
findings.body: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb no longer defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, or :private_category. Those definitions were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, and Fabricator(:embeddable_host) was written into the category file. Autoloading every fabricator file may hide this, but any explicit load of category_fabricator.rb will not define categories, and putting the category fabricators back in the original file without removing the copy will raise a duplicate fabricator error. The files need to be swapped back before merge.

findings.title: New admin endpoints and the migration are untested
findings.body: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only assert the class ancestry. They never POST/PUT/DELETE, so a missing id 500, a nil host, invalid category_id, and the uncategorized fallback are not exercised. There is no migration spec, so the empty embed_category crash and the un-normalized host INSERT would not be caught. EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? examples use only lowercase hosts and do not cover mixed-case referers, ports, or scheme-prefixed values of the kind the old site setting accepted.
